    17	#   test names added inline.

    20	#   boundary note: the invariant applies to new runs; a resume continues the

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Tests: --from-stage <s> rehydrates completed-stage artifacts before dispatching <s>.
     3	# (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5 / _runner_from_stage_preflight)
     4	#
     5	# SPEC-3 [code]: --from-stage <s> rehydrates all stages before <s> via
     6	#   _artifact_persist_restore and _artifact_persist_put_back, places their
     7	#   artifacts in ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR, dispatches <s> as the first stage, and
     8	#   emits no stage.start for any earlier stage.

    10	# SPEC-4 [code]: --from-stage <s> when a stage before <s> has no restorable

    12	#   in stderr.

   101

   105	_s13_loop_fixt_content="$(cat "$FIXT/cycle-converges-iter2.yaml")"
   106	assert_contains "[#1805/SPEC-13] cycle fixture used by resume-loop-state test has type: cycle" \

   112	assert_gt \

   116	cleanup_test_env
   117	print_test_results

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Tests: all three resume entry paths invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before
     3	# the dispatch loop. (issue #1805, ADR-006 §3.5)
     4	#
     5	# SPEC-9 [code]: All three resume entry paths (--resume flag to runner.sh,
     6	#   auto-resume on detecting status=interrupted, zbuild pipeline resume
     7	#   --run-id) invoke _runner_resume_rehydrate before the dispatch loop.
     8	#   Its test must FAIL on the code as it was before this change.
     9	#
    10	# Three sub-tests, each with a separate work repo, state dir, and events dir:
    11	#   Path 1 — bash runner.sh --resume
    12	#   Path 2 — bash runner.sh (no --resume; state status=interrupted → auto_resume)
    13	#   Path 3 — bash zbuild pipeline resume --run-id
    14	#
    15	# Discriminating assertion for all paths: intake-result.json is present in
    16	# ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR after the runner call (artifact restored from state branch).
    17	# Before this change: no rehydration → artifact absent → FAILS.
    18	# After this change: _runner_resume_rehydrate restores it → PASSES.
    19	set -euo pipefail
    20	
    21	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    22	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"

    30	# shellcheck source=../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
    31	source "$REPO_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"
    32

    34	setup_test_env "resume-entry-points-1805"

    36

    39	mock_plugin_factory "build"  "agent" 0 >/dev/null
    40	# cycled sub-stage used by the artifact-snapshot-coverage cyclic fixture (SPEC-13 sub-case).
    41	mock_plugin_factory "cycled" "agent" 0 "" "builder" >/dev/null
    42	PLUGINS_ROOT="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/plugins"
    43	
    44	# ── Shared helper: set up a work repo with a state branch for one path ──────────
    45	# Usage: _setup_path_state <label> <issue_id> → sets:
    46	#   P_WORK_REPO, P_STATE_DIR, P_STATE_FILE, P_EVENTS_DIR, P_EVENTS_JSONL
    47	_setup_path_state() {
    48	    local label="$1" issue_id="$2"
    49	
    50	    P_WORK_REPO="$(setup_git_temp_repo "ep-${label}")"
    51	    install_template_overlay "$P_WORK_REPO" runner-state-dir-minimal
    52	
    53	    P_STATE_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-state"
    54	    P_EVENTS_DIR="$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-events"
    55	    P_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_DIR/pipeline-state.json"
    56	    P_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_DIR/events.jsonl"
    57	    mkdir -p "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts" "$P_EVENTS_DIR"
    58	
    59	    # Write the intake artifact so the snapshot captures it.
    60	    printf '{"result_contract":3,"outcome":"pass","reason":"prior-run intake"}' \
    61	        > "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"

    65	    ( export ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
    66	      cd "$P_WORK_REPO" && _artifact_persist_snapshot "$P_STATE_DIR" "$issue_id" ) \
    67	        >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>&1 || _snap_rc=$?
    68	    if [[ "$_snap_rc" -ne 0 ]]; then

    70	            "rc=$_snap_rc; $(cat "$TEST_TEMP_DIR/${label}-snap.log" 2>/dev/null | tail -5)"
    71	    fi
    72

    74	    rm -f "$P_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
    75	}

    77	# ── PATH 1: --resume flag to runner.sh ────────────────────────────────────────
    78	print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 1: bash runner.sh --resume restores artifacts"
    79	
    80	P1_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"

    82	P1_WORK_REPO="$P_WORK_REPO"
    83	P1_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
    84	P1_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_FILE"
    85	P1_EVENTS_DIR="$P_EVENTS_DIR"
    86	P1_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_JSONL"
    87	
    88	jq -n \
    89	    --arg run_id "s9-p1-resume-1805" \
    90	    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    91	    --argjson issue "$P1_ID" \
    92	    '{
    93	        schema_version: 1,
    94	        run_id: $run_id,
    95	        issue: $issue,
    96	        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
    97	        current_iteration: 0,
    98	        self_heal_count: {},
    99	        scope_manifest_hash: "",

   104	        updated_at: $now

   111	    ZBUILD_STATE_DIR="$P1_STATE_DIR" \
   112	    ZBUILD_STATE_FILE="$P1_STATE_FILE" \
   113	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_DIR="$P1_EVENTS_DIR" \
   114	    ZBUILD_EVENTS_JSONL="$P1_EVENTS_JSONL" \
   115	    ZBUILD_EVENT_SCHEMA="$REPO_ROOT/config/event-schema.json" \
   116	    ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn \
   117	    ZBUILD_VISION_GATE=off \
   118	    PATH="$PATH" HOME="$HOME" \
   119	    bash "$RUNNER" --template runner-state-dir-minimal \
   120	        --resume --issue "$P1_ID" ) \
   121	    >"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1-stdout.txt" 2>"$TEST_TEMP_DIR/p1-stderr.txt"
   122	set -e

   124	# [#1805/SPEC-9] path 1 assertion: artifact restored.
   125	# Before change: no rehydration → file absent → FAILS.
   126	# After change: _runner_resume_rehydrate restores it → PASSES.
   127	assert_file_exists \
   128	    "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 1 (--resume flag): intake-result.json restored from state branch" \
   129	    "$P1_STATE_DIR/artifacts/intake-result.json"
   130	
   131	# ── PATH 2: auto-resume on detecting status=interrupted ───────────────────────
   132	print_test_section "[#1805/SPEC-9] path 2: auto-resume on status=interrupted restores artifacts"
   133	
   134	P2_ID="$(zb_test_issue)"
   135	_setup_path_state "p2" "$P2_ID"
   136	P2_WORK_REPO="$P_WORK_REPO"
   137	P2_STATE_DIR="$P_STATE_DIR"
   138	P2_STATE_FILE="$P_STATE_FILE"
   139	P2_EVENTS_DIR="$P_EVENTS_DIR"
   140	P2_EVENTS_JSONL="$P_EVENTS_JSONL"
   141	
   142	# status=interrupted → get_resume_recommendation → auto_resume → resume_mode=true.
   143	jq -n \
   144	    --arg run_id "s9-p2-resume-1805" \
   145	    --arg now "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
   146	    --argjson issue "$P2_ID" \
   147	    '{
   148	        schema_version: 1,
   149	        run_id: $run_id,
   150	        issue: $issue,
   151	        stage_statuses: {intake: "complete", build: "pending"},
   152	        current_iteration: 0,
   153	        self_heal_count: {},
   154	        scope_manifest_hash: "",
   155	        cost_ledger_pointer: 0,
   156	        claim_lease_id: "",

# ─── _artifact_persist_restore <issue> <restored_dir> [repo_root] ───────────
# Extract the tip of the state branch into <restored_dir> (created if absent).
# Prefers a local refs/heads/<branch>; falls back to refs/remotes/origin/<branch>
# when only the fetched remote ref is present (CI). No-op (rc 0, empty dir) when
# no state branch exists. Never touches the working tree.
_artifact_persist_restore() {
    _artifact_persist_reset_status
    local issue="${1:-0}" restored_dir="$2" repo_root="${3:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)}"
    # Resolve the SHARED git dir (see _artifact_persist_git_dir). Two reasons:
    #   1. refs must be read from the shared store, not a per-worktree view;
    #   2. the old guard tested `-d "$repo_root/.git"`, which is FALSE in a linked
    #      worktree because .git is a file there — restore would silently no-op and
    #      prior artifacts would never come back, with no error to notice.
    local _gd=""
    [[ -n "$repo_root" ]] && _artifact_persist_git_dir_v _gd "$repo_root"
    [[ -z "$restored_dir" ]] && { _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no restored_dir given"; return 2; }
    if [[ -z "$repo_root" || ! -d "$_gd" ]]; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="unresolvable repo: repo_root=[${repo_root:-<empty>}] git_dir=[${_gd:-<empty>}] cwd=[$PWD]"
        return 1
    fi

    local branch; _artifact_persist_branch_v branch "$issue"
    local ref=""
    if GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/heads/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ref="refs/heads/$branch"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="local"
    elif GIT_DIR="$_gd" git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/remotes/origin/$branch" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        ref="refs/remotes/origin/$branch"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE="remote"
    else
        # A first-ever run for this issue. Genuinely nothing to restore — the one
        # early return here that is NOT a failure.
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="empty"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no $branch locally or on origin (first run)"
        return 0
    fi

    if ! mkdir -p "$restored_dir"; then
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="mkdir -p $restored_dir failed"
        return 1
    fi
    # git archive streams the tree; tar unpacks it, no checkout / index change.
    # #1878: PIPESTATUS, not the pipeline rc — a failing `git archive` piped into
    # a happy `tar` yields rc=0, so a broken restore reported success.
    # PR #1880 review: guarded (see the _ct_err note above).
    local _ar_err; _ar_err="$(mktemp -u "$(zbuild_engine_tmpdir)/zbuild-restore-err.XXXXXX" 2>/dev/null)" || _ar_err="/dev/null"
    [[ -n "$_ar_err" ]] || _ar_err="/dev/null"
    GIT_DIR="$_gd" git archive "$ref" 2>"$_ar_err" | tar -x -C "$restored_dir" 2>>"$_ar_err"
    local _st=("${PIPESTATUS[@]}")
    if [[ "${_st[0]}" -ne 0 || "${_st[1]}" -ne 0 ]]; then
        local err; err="$(cat "$_ar_err" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
        rm -f "$_ar_err"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restore of $ref failed (archive rc=${_st[0]} tar rc=${_st[1]}): ${err:-<no stderr>}"
        return 1
    fi
    rm -f "$_ar_err"
    # PR #1880 review: "restored", NOT "saved". The same channel carries both
    # operations' outcomes, so reusing "saved" would let a caller checking
    # `== "saved"` to confirm a SNAPSHOT be satisfied by a restore that happened
    # to run first — the restore runs once at startup, before any snapshot.
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="restored"
    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="restored from $ref"
    return 0

2	# plugins/tool/hydrate/plugin.sh — Hydrate stage (#1074, ADR-050 §7, ADR-059 §3)
3	#
4	# Kind: tool  Tier: T0  (NO LLM calls — NEVER call route_to_model)
5	#
6	# Puts this issue's earlier outputs, saved on `zbuild/state/issue-<N>`, back in
7	# their LIVE places in the run's artifacts folder. First stage in the flow,
8	# before intake. A rerun of an issue continues it (ADR-050, amended; ADR-068
9	# §8): an earlier run's output is that stage's latest output until the stage
10	# writes a newer one, so there is one place to read and no "restored" area.
11	# A file the run already has live is newer and is kept.
12	#
13	# A PARTIAL TREE IS NEVER PUT BACK. `git archive | tar` can fail mid-stream
14	# (disk full, permissions) leaving a half-extracted tree. PR #1880's review
15	# caught the engine adopting one. Extraction goes to a staging dir and only a
16	# complete one is copied into place.
17	
18	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
19	_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_LOADED=1

22	source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh"
23	zbuild_plugin_bootstrap "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"

25	source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/stage-summary.sh"

27	# shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/stage-result.sh
28	source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/stage-result.sh"
29	_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT="$_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_ROOT"

32	source "$_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
33	# shellcheck source=../../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
34	source "$_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"
35	# shellcheck source=../../../core/state/atomic.sh
36	source "$_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT/core/state/atomic.sh"
37	
38	# ─── _hydrate_fetch <issue> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
39	# Make origin's copy of the state branch available locally.
40	#
41	# WHY: `_artifact_persist_restore` reads `refs/heads/<branch>` first and
42	# `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` second. On a fresh clone — which every CI
43	# runner is — NEITHER exists until something fetches, so restore reports "first
44	# run" for an issue that has plenty of prior work. That is the half of ADR-050
45	# that only ever worked because the CI workflow fetched the branch itself in a
46	# `run:` block; doing it here is what makes local and CI one mechanism.
47	#
48	# Fetch updates the REMOTE-TRACKING ref only. It never moves `refs/heads`, so a
49	# local snapshot that was never pushed survives this untouched — which is the
50	# point: preferring origin over unpushed local work would lose that work.
51	_hydrate_fetch() {
52	    local issue="$1"
53	    local branch; branch="$(_artifact_persist_branch "$issue")"
54	    git remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
55	    git fetch --quiet --no-tags origin \
56	        "+refs/heads/${branch}:refs/remotes/origin/${branch}" 2>/dev/null
57	}
58	
59	# ─── _hydrate_put_back <from> <to> ───────────────────────────────────────────
60	# Copy every file under <from> to the same place under <to>, skipping any file
61	# <to> already has. One file at a time rather than `cp -n`, whose exit status on
62	# a skipped file differs between BSD and newer GNU coreutils. stage-io/ is left
63	# out: it records one run's model calls and is no stage's output.
64	_hydrate_put_back() {
65	    local from="$1" to="$2" f rel
66	    mkdir -p "$to" || return 1
67	    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
68	        rel="${f#"$from"/}"
69	        [[ "$rel" == stage-io/* || -e "$to/$rel" ]] && continue
70	        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$to/$rel")" && cp -p "$f" "$to/$rel" || return 1
71	    done < <(find "$from" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
72	    return 0
73	}
74	
75	# ─── hydrate_run <stage_id> <state_file> ─────────────────────────────────────
76	hydrate_run() {
77	    local _stage_id="${1:-hydrate}"
78	    local _state_file="${2:-}"
79	
80	    local _issue="${ZBUILD_ISSUE_NUMBER:-${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}}"
81	    local _state_dir
82	    if [[ -n "$_state_file" ]]; then
83	        _state_dir="$(dirname "$_state_file")"
84	    else
85	        _state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
86	    fi
87	    local _artifacts_dir="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$_state_dir/artifacts}"
88	
89	    emit_event "hydrate.start" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
90	
91	    if ! _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_issue"; then
92	        # Neither an issue nor a goal: no identity, so nothing to hydrate from.
93	        # A --goal run DOES have one (#1931) and no longer lands here.
94	        _hydrate_write_result "$_artifacts_dir" "pass" \
95	            "no identity — neither an issue nor a goal" "skipped" 0
96	        emit_event "hydrate.complete" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
97	            "restored=0" "reason=no_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
98	        return 0
99	    fi
100	
101	    # The engine derives and exports this; we only fill it. Recomputing the same
102	    # expression here rather than inventing one keeps the two halves from
103	    # drifting — a boundary whose halves disagree about where something lives is
104	    # not a boundary (#1809).
105	    # #2225: --no-resume recreates — nothing from a prior run is restored. The
106	    # saved history is still fetched and adopted (below), so the next snapshot
107	    # extends it rather than force-pushing a new one over it (review #2229).
108	    if [[ "${ZBUILD_RESUME:-1}" == "0" ]]; then
109	        if ! _hydrate_fetch "$_issue"; then
110	            emit_event "hydrate.fetch.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
111	        fi
112	        if ! _artifact_persist_adopt_remote "$_issue"; then
113	            emit_event "hydrate.adopt.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
114	                "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
115	        fi
116	        _hydrate_write_result "$_artifacts_dir" "pass" \
117	            "fresh start (--no-resume): prior work not restored; the saved history is kept" "skipped" 0
118	        emit_event "hydrate.complete" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
119	            "restored=0" "reason=no_resume" 2>/dev/null || true
120	        return 0
121	    fi
122	
123	    local _staging="$_state_dir/hydrate.staging"
124	
125	    if ! _hydrate_fetch "$_issue"; then
126	        # Not fatal, and not silent. An offline developer still hydrates from a
127	        # local snapshot; a CI runner does not, and needs to see why.
128	        emit_event "hydrate.fetch.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
129	    fi

131	    rm -rf "$_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
132	    # #2366: pass, or fail when prior work exists but could not be put back.
133	    local _verdict="pass" _reason="" _status="empty" _count=0 _source=""

135	    if _artifact_persist_restore "$_issue" "$_staging"; then
136	        _status="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-unknown}"

138	        # _artifact_persist_adopt_remote below resets it. #1921.
139	        _source="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE:-}"
140	    else
141	        _status="failed"
142	        _verdict="fail"

144	        # (`repo_root=… git_dir=… cwd=…`), which differ between two runs of the
145	        # same pipeline — the parity test caught exactly that. ADR-016 also
146	        # lists path leakage as mandatory: a result artifact can be quoted into
147	        # a GitHub comment. The detail still reaches the operator, on the event
148	        # and the warn below, which stay local.
149	        _reason="restore failed (see hydrate.restore.failed)"
150	        emit_event "hydrate.restore.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
151	            "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
152	        warn "hydrate: restore failed: ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
153	    fi
154	
155	    # Put back ONLY a complete extraction. On failure the staging tree is
156	    # discarded whole — a half-restored artifact set seeded into a stage is
157	    # worse than no prior work at all (PR #1880 review). No-clobber: a live
158	    # file is this run's own, and newer.
159	    if [[ "$_status" != "failed" && -d "$_staging/artifacts" ]] \
160	       && [[ -n "$(ls -A "$_staging/artifacts" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
161	        _count="$(find "$_staging/artifacts" -type f 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c . || printf '0')"

174	    # Give the snapshot a parent to chain onto. A fetch only ever writes
175	    # refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, so on a CI runner refs/heads never exists —

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# plugins/tool/hydrate/plugin.sh — Hydrate stage (#1074, ADR-050 §7, ADR-059 §3)
#
# Kind: tool  Tier: T0  (NO LLM calls — NEVER call route_to_model)
#
# Puts this issue's earlier outputs, saved on `zbuild/state/issue-<N>`, back in
# their LIVE places in the run's artifacts folder. First stage in the flow,
# before intake. A rerun of an issue continues it (ADR-050, amended; ADR-068
# §8): an earlier run's output is that stage's latest output until the stage
# writes a newer one, so there is one place to read and no "restored" area.
# A file the run already has live is newer and is kept.
#
# A PARTIAL TREE IS NEVER PUT BACK. `git archive | tar` can fail mid-stream
# (disk full, permissions) leaving a half-extracted tree. PR #1880's review
# caught the engine adopting one. Extraction goes to a staging dir and only a
# complete one is copied into place.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_LOADED=1

# shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh
source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/plugin-bootstrap.sh"
zbuild_plugin_bootstrap "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
# shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/stage-summary.sh
source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/stage-summary.sh"
# #2366 (ADR-054 §6): the one result writer — contract 3, one outcome.
# shellcheck source=../../../scripts/lib/stage-result.sh
source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; pwd)/../../../scripts/lib/stage-result.sh"
_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT="$_ZBUILD_PLUGIN_ROOT"

# shellcheck source=../../../core/event-bus/event-bus.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT/core/event-bus/event-bus.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../../core/state/artifact-persist.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT/core/state/artifact-persist.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../../core/state/atomic.sh
source "$_ZBUILD_HYDRATE_ROOT/core/state/atomic.sh"

# ─── _hydrate_fetch <issue> ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Make origin's copy of the state branch available locally.
#
# WHY: `_artifact_persist_restore` reads `refs/heads/<branch>` first and
# `refs/remotes/origin/<branch>` second. On a fresh clone — which every CI
# runner is — NEITHER exists until something fetches, so restore reports "first
# run" for an issue that has plenty of prior work. That is the half of ADR-050
# that only ever worked because the CI workflow fetched the branch itself in a
# `run:` block; doing it here is what makes local and CI one mechanism.
#
# Fetch updates the REMOTE-TRACKING ref only. It never moves `refs/heads`, so a
# local snapshot that was never pushed survives this untouched — which is the
# point: preferring origin over unpushed local work would lose that work.
_hydrate_fetch() {
    local issue="$1"
    local branch; branch="$(_artifact_persist_branch "$issue")"
    git remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    git fetch --quiet --no-tags origin \
        "+refs/heads/${branch}:refs/remotes/origin/${branch}" 2>/dev/null
}

# ─── _hydrate_put_back <from> <to> ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Copy every file under <from> to the same place under <to>, skipping any file
# <to> already has. One file at a time rather than `cp -n`, whose exit status on
# a skipped file differs between BSD and newer GNU coreutils. stage-io/ is left
# out: it records one run's model calls and is no stage's output.
_hydrate_put_back() {
    local from="$1" to="$2" f rel
    mkdir -p "$to" || return 1
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        rel="${f#"$from"/}"
        [[ "$rel" == stage-io/* || -e "$to/$rel" ]] && continue
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$to/$rel")" && cp -p "$f" "$to/$rel" || return 1
    done < <(find "$from" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
    return 0
}

# ─── hydrate_run <stage_id> <state_file> ─────────────────────────────────────
hydrate_run() {
    local _stage_id="${1:-hydrate}"
    local _state_file="${2:-}"

    local _issue="${ZBUILD_ISSUE_NUMBER:-${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}}"
    local _state_dir
    if [[ -n "$_state_file" ]]; then
        _state_dir="$(dirname "$_state_file")"
    else
        _state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    fi
    local _artifacts_dir="${ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR:-$_state_dir/artifacts}"

    emit_event "hydrate.start" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" 2>/dev/null || true

    if ! _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_issue"; then
        # Neither an issue nor a goal: no identity, so nothing to hydrate from.
        # A --goal run DOES have one (#1931) and no longer lands here.
        _hydrate_write_result "$_artifacts_dir" "pass" \
            "no identity — neither an issue nor a goal" "skipped" 0
        emit_event "hydrate.complete" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
            "restored=0" "reason=no_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
    fi

    # The engine derives and exports this; we only fill it. Recomputing the same
    # expression here rather than inventing one keeps the two halves from
    # drifting — a boundary whose halves disagree about where something lives is
    # not a boundary (#1809).
    # #2225: --no-resume recreates — nothing from a prior run is restored. The
    # saved history is still fetched and adopted (below), so the next snapshot
    # extends it rather than force-pushing a new one over it (review #2229).
    if [[ "${ZBUILD_RESUME:-1}" == "0" ]]; then
        if ! _hydrate_fetch "$_issue"; then
            emit_event "hydrate.fetch.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        if ! _artifact_persist_adopt_remote "$_issue"; then
            emit_event "hydrate.adopt.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
                "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        _hydrate_write_result "$_artifacts_dir" "pass" \
            "fresh start (--no-resume): prior work not restored; the saved history is kept" "skipped" 0
        emit_event "hydrate.complete" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
            "restored=0" "reason=no_resume" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
    fi

    local _staging="$_state_dir/hydrate.staging"

    if ! _hydrate_fetch "$_issue"; then
        # Not fatal, and not silent. An offline developer still hydrates from a
        # local snapshot; a CI runner does not, and needs to see why.
        emit_event "hydrate.fetch.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

    rm -rf "$_staging" 2>/dev/null || true
    # #2366: pass, or fail when prior work exists but could not be put back.
    local _verdict="pass" _reason="" _status="empty" _count=0 _source=""

    if _artifact_persist_restore "$_issue" "$_staging"; then
        _status="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-unknown}"
        # Read the source BEFORE anything else touches the outcome channel:
        # _artifact_persist_adopt_remote below resets it. #1921.
        _source="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SOURCE:-}"
    else
        _status="failed"
        _verdict="fail"
        # PATH-FREE on purpose. The library's reason embeds absolute paths
        # (`repo_root=… git_dir=… cwd=…`), which differ between two runs of the
        # same pipeline — the parity test caught exactly that. ADR-016 also
        # lists path leakage as mandatory: a result artifact can be quoted into
        # a GitHub comment. The detail still reaches the operator, on the event
        # and the warn below, which stay local.
        _reason="restore failed (see hydrate.restore.failed)"
        emit_event "hydrate.restore.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
            "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
        warn "hydrate: restore failed: ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
    fi

    # Put back ONLY a complete extraction. On failure the staging tree is
    # discarded whole — a half-restored artifact set seeded into a stage is
    # worse than no prior work at all (PR #1880 review). No-clobber: a live
    # file is this run's own, and newer.
    if [[ "$_status" != "failed" && -d "$_staging/artifacts" ]] \
       && [[ -n "$(ls -A "$_staging/artifacts" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then
        _count="$(find "$_staging/artifacts" -type f 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep -c . || printf '0')"
        if _hydrate_put_back "$_staging/artifacts" "$_artifacts_dir"; then
            [[ -n "$_reason" ]] || _reason="restored $_count artifact(s) from zbuild/state/issue-$_issue"
        else
            _verdict="fail"
            _reason="restored tree could not be put in place"
            _count=0
        fi
    else
        [[ -n "$_reason" ]] || _reason="no prior work for issue $_issue (first run)"
    fi
    rm -rf "${_staging:?}" 2>/dev/null || true

    # Give the snapshot a parent to chain onto. A fetch only ever writes
    # refs/remotes/origin/<branch>, so on a CI runner refs/heads never exists —
    # _artifact_persist_snapshot then roots a new history and the force-push
    # orphans everything already on origin (#1921). Adopt is absent-only, so the
    # unpushed-local-work invariant above is untouched. Deliberately AFTER the
    # restore, whose source we captured before this resets the channel.
    if ! _artifact_persist_adopt_remote "$_issue"; then
        emit_event "hydrate.adopt.failed" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
            "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

    _hydrate_write_result "$_artifacts_dir" "$_verdict" "$_reason" "$_status" "$_count" "$_source"
    emit_event "hydrate.complete" "stage=$_stage_id" "issue=$_issue" \
        "restored=$_count" "status=$_status" "source=${_source:-none}" 2>/dev/null || true
    # Always 0. Prior work is an optimisation: a run that cannot find any still
    # has everything it needs to do the work from scratch.
    return 0
}

_hydrate_write_result() {
    local _dir="$1" _verdict="$2" _reason="$3" _status="$4" _count="$5" _src="${6:-}"
    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
    local _file="$_dir/hydrate-result.json"
    if ! stage_result_write "$_file" "$_verdict" "${_reason:-no detail}" \
            "$(jq -nc --arg s "$_status" --argjson c "${_count:-0}" --arg src "$_src" \
                '{status: $s, restored: $c, source: (if $src == "" then null else $src end)}')"; then
        emit_event "hydrate.result.write_failed" "file=$_file" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    # ADR-055 §9: every hydrate terminal funnels through here, and the real
    # counts are already in hand.
    stage_summary_write "$_dir/hydrate-summary.md" "hydrate" "$_verdict" \
        "restored ${_count:-0} artifact(s) from prior runs (${_status:-unknown})" \
        "$(printf -- '- source: %s\n- detail: %s' "${_src:-none}" "${_reason:-none}")"
}

trap '_runner_signal_trap TERM' TERM

    # Detect platforms (writes state/platforms.json; returns "generic" if none found)
    local _DETECTED_PLATFORMS=()
    while IFS= read -r p; do
        [[ -n "$p" ]] && _DETECTED_PLATFORMS+=("$p")
    done < <(detect_platforms "$PWD" "$state_dir" 2>/dev/null)
    [[ ${#_DETECTED_PLATFORMS[@]} -eq 0 ]] && _DETECTED_PLATFORMS=("generic")

        # in `_runner_abort_trap`, but a hard kill (-9), host crash, or any
        # path that skipped the EXIT trap can leave a stale .abort.signal.
        # Without this disarm the first `_zbuild_check_abort` pre-flight in
        # the dispatch loop would observe the stale sentinel and abort the
        # resumed run immediately. Resume must always start from a clean
        # signal channel.
        _zbuild_disarm_abort_sentinel

            "engine_sha=$_eng_sha" "engine_branch=$_eng_br"

1	# ADR-006: Resume Contract — Pipeline-Resume Memory
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	**Date:** 2026-05-24
5	
6	> **Memory type:** This ADR governs **pipeline-resume memory** — the operational
7	> state needed to continue an interrupted pipeline from where it stopped (which
8	> stage failed, which iteration counter, which checkpoint, scope manifest hash,
9	> plugin state, claim lease). It is one of zBuild's **two distinct memory models**:
10	>
11	> | Memory type | Purpose | Where defined | Backend |
12	> |---|---|---|---|
13	> | **Pipeline-resume memory** | Continue an interrupted pipeline at the failure point | ADR-006 (this), transported by ADR-010 cache | Always-on; baked into core/state/ |
14	> | **Learning memory** | Remember patterns, embeddings, decisions across pipelines and runs | [ADR-011](ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md) | Pluggable: sqlite default, ruflo HNSW optional |
15	>
16	> The two are independent: a pipeline can resume cleanly with no learning
17	> memory available, and learning memory persists across pipelines whether or
18	> not a particular pipeline ever resumed.
19	
20	## Context
21	
22	The legacy resume semantics are partially documented. `resume_state` in `legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-state.sh:876-1075` restores stage statuses and `SELF_HEAL_COUNT` but **does not** read back `CURRENT_ITERATION` — verified at line 269 (written) and confirmed absent in lines 987-1026 (read). On resume, plugins relying on iteration count receive the *initial* value (often 0), causing the loop to re-do iterations.
23	
24	Other state that doesn't survive resume:
25	- `loop-state.md` (gitignored; per-iteration debug state; regenerated each run).
26	- Runtime caches (computed git diffs, environment snapshots, router recommendations).
27	- Scope-violation diagnostic logs (if `persist_artifacts` failed mid-write).
28	
29	This isn't a bug per se; it's a contract that was never written down. Plugins inherit different assumptions: some assume iteration is durable; some assume it's reconstructed; some don't think about it at all. The result is brittle resume behavior.
30	
31	## Decision
32	
33	zBuild's resume contract is explicit. Two tiers: **persisted** (engine guarantees survival) and **reconstructed** (engine or plugin recomputes at the start of `run` after resume — ADR-056 deleted the `init` hook that used to own this).
34	
35	### Persisted (engine-managed, atomic_write + .bak rotation)
36	
37	| Key | Owner | Type | Notes |
38	|---|---|---|---|
39	| `stage_statuses[]` | core/state | enum per stage | `pending`/`in_progress`/`complete`/`failed`/`skipped` |
40	| `current_iteration` | core/state | int | **NEW in zBuild** — fixes legacy resume gap |
41	| `self_heal_count` | core/state | int | per-stage retry counter |
42	| `scope_manifest_hash` | core/redaction | sha256 | detects scope-manifest mutation across resume |
43	| `cost_ledger_pointer` | core/cost | offset into ledger | enables resume to continue cost tracking |
44	| `plugin_state[plugin_id]` | per-plugin | opaque blob | plugin-declared state (see below) |
45	| `claim_lease_id` | core/locks | string | required for claim-coordinator's `heartbeat` after resume |
46	| ~~`events_db`~~ | core/event-bus | — | retired (amended 2026-10-24, ADR-065 §5): the SQLite mirror had no reader and was removed; the event history is `events.jsonl` |
47	
48	All persisted state is written via `core/state/atomic_write`, which:
49	1. Disk-space precheck.
50	2. `flock` on a sidecar `.lock` file.
51	3. `mktemp` + write + `fsync`.
52	4. `mv` (atomic on POSIX).
53	5. Rotate previous to `.bak`.
54	
55	> **Amended 2026-10-24 ([ADR-065](ADR-065-process-budget.md) §5).** No disk-space precheck: a full
56	> disk fails the write itself, which leaves the target untouched and says so. The temp file is
57	> opened by the shell with noclobber (exclusive, as `mktemp`'s was). The `.bak` is rotated only by
58	> the state writers (`atomic_write --bak`, used by `locked_state_update` and `init_state`), the
59	> only files the `.bak` recovery reads; other files keep no `.bak`.
60	>
61	> **Amended 2026-10-25 (ADR-065 §5, round 5).** The temp file is opened with the mode it must end
62	> with (the target's, or 0600 for a new file), so no `chmod` follows unless the mode has an
63	> execute bit. `atomic_replace` makes its unique temp name in the shell and claims it with
64	> noclobber, and copies with `cp -p`, so a state file's `.bak` keeps the state's 0600. Guarded by
65	> `tests/unit/atomic-write-cost-test.sh` W1/W3 and `tests/unit/helpers-cost-test.sh` H2/H3.
66	
67	Reads use `validate_json`; corruption triggers `.bak` recovery. (KEEPERS §C additions 1–2 lift these into the hot path.)
68	
69	### Reconstructed (computed at the start of `run` after resume)
70	
71	| Key | Owner | How |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| `git_diff` | per-stage | `git diff` against baseline |
74	| `repo_hash` | core/state | hash of `git rev-parse HEAD` |
75	| `env_snapshot` | per-stage | captured in the `run` preamble |
76	| `router_recommendations` | core/router | recomputed from cost ledger + outcomes |
77	| `scope_violations_history` | per-stage | replayed from event bus |
78	| `loop_state_md` | debug | regenerated each iteration |
79	
80	### Plugin responsibilities
81	
82	Every plugin's `manifest.yaml` MUST declare:
83	
84	```yaml
85	state:
86	  persisted: [findings, last_cycle_score]    # keys to write via core/state
87	  reconstructed: [git_diff, repo_hash]        # keys to recompute in the run preamble
88	```
89	
90	The engine validates:
91	1. Every key in `persisted` has a corresponding `core/state/write_plugin_state <plugin_id> <key> <value>` call in `plugin.sh` (greppable; loose but catches obvious omissions).
92	2. Every key in `reconstructed` is set by the `run` preamble before the stage does any work. Asserted at runtime: missing keys → plugin refuses to run.
93	
94	### Idempotency scope for `run`
95	
96	"Plugins MUST be idempotent across re-runs of `run`" means:
97	
98	- **In scope (A — what is guaranteed):** within a *single resume operation* on a *single pipeline-state.json*, the engine may call `run` more than once (e.g., the cycle re-enters the stage after a transient failure). The plugin MUST tolerate this: side-effects must be writable-or-reread without duplication. Concretely: writing to `core/state/write_plugin_state` is idempotent because the engine de-duplicates; writing to an external sink (Slack, GitHub comment) is NOT idempotent and MUST be guarded by a sentinel key in persisted state.
99	- **Out of scope (B — what is NOT guaranteed):** idempotency across *different* pipeline runs (run A resumes, then unrelated run B starts). Run B starts fresh; the plugin's `run` may legitimately re-emit side-effects from run B even if run A already did so. Cross-run de-duplication is the calling system's concern (e.g., GitHub issue body de-dup belongs in the output-destination layer, not in the plugin).
100	
101	**Worked example.** `security-lens` declares `persisted: [last_pr_comment_id]`. On its first `run`, it posts a comment, captures the comment ID, writes it via `core/state/write_plugin_state`. On a second `run` *within the same resume*, it reads the persisted ID, sees the comment exists, skips the post. On a `run` for a different pipeline run, it has no persisted ID for that run and posts again — that's correct, because the runs are independent artifacts.
102	
103	### Resume sequence
104	
105	```
106	1. core/state load(pipeline-state.json) → on error: try .bak; on .bak error: refuse to resume
107	2. core/state restore persisted state into runtime
108	3. For each plugin in dependency order:
109	   a. call plugin.run with ZBUILD_RESUMING=1 (ADR-056 deleted the init hook;
110	      reconstruction is the run preamble's job)
111	   b. plugin reads persisted state via core/state/read_plugin_state
112	   c. plugin recomputes reconstructed state
113	   d. plugin refuses to continue if any reconstructed key is missing
114	4. Engine emits "pipeline.resume" event
115	5. Continue from last in_progress stage
116	```
117	
118	### Best-effort contract
119	
120	Resume is best-effort, not transparent. The engine guarantees:
121	- All `persisted` keys survive.
122	- All `reconstructed` keys are recomputed before any plugin observes them.
123	- If recomputation fails, the engine refuses to resume and exits with a clear error (no silent half-resume).
124	
125	The engine does NOT guarantee:
126	- Identical behavior to an uninterrupted run (LLM nondeterminism makes this impossible).
127	- Cost equivalence (resume re-enters `run` and may re-route models).
128	- Wall-clock continuity (the resume adds startup latency).
129	
130	## Consequences
131	
132	**Good:**
133	- Fixes the legacy `CURRENT_ITERATION` resume gap explicitly.
134	- Plugin authors have a checklist: declare persisted, declare reconstructed, write tests.
135	- Resume failures are loud and explicit; no silent half-state.
136	- `kill -9` → restart works for any well-behaved plugin.
137	
138	**Bad:**
139	- Manifest authorship friction (one more section to declare).
140	- Reconstructed state can be expensive to recompute (e.g., large git diffs). Mitigation: plugins can cache reconstructed state into persisted state if they declare both.
141	- The "every persisted key has a write_plugin_state call" check is grep-based, not type-checked. Accepted as a soft guardrail.
142	
143	## Amendment — `preflight_failed` pipeline status (issue #496, ADR-020)
144	
145	ADR-020 introduces a pre-flight inter-stage data contract validator that
146	runs at pipeline start (after `load_template`, before any stage executes).
147	When the validator fails in `ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce` mode, the
148	runner writes a minimal state.json with `status: preflight_failed` so
149	operators can distinguish "pipeline halted before any stage ran" from
150	"pipeline interrupted mid-flight."
151	
152	The pipeline status enum now includes:
153	
154	| Value | Set by | Meaning |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| `in_progress` | runner | stages running |
157	| `complete` | runner | all stages succeeded |
158	| `interrupted` | runner | aborted mid-flight (signal, mid-stage failure) |
159	| `aborted` | runner / operator | explicit cancellation |
160	| `failed` | runner | terminal failure after at least one stage ran |
161	| `preflight_failed` | contract-validator (ADR-020) | rejected before any stage; no resume target |
162	| `timed_out` | runner watchdog (ADR-054 §11) | run exceeded per-run wall-clock limit; resumable |
163	
164	Pipelines in `preflight_failed` status are NOT resumable; the runner's
165	resume policy refuses to restart them (the contract violation is in the
166	template or manifests, not in execution state). The resume command should
167	surface a "fix the contract first" hint rather than attempting to continue.
168	
169	## Amendment — `cycle_iterations` persistence (issue #512, ADR-021)
170	
171	ADR-021 introduces the outer-cycle orchestrator. Cycle state is persisted
172	under a new schema-additive key on `pipeline-state.json`:
173	
174	```json
175	"cycle_iterations": {
176	  "<cycle_id>": {
177	    "status": "in_progress|complete|plateau|divergence|max_iterations|verdict_missing|aborted|preflight_failed",
178	    "current_iter": <N>,
179	    "max_iterations": <M>,
180	    "history_file": "<state_dir>/cycle-<id>-history.jsonl",
181	    "iter": [...]
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	`stage_statuses[]` enum is **unchanged**. Per-cycle stage outcome lives
187	under `cycle_iterations[X].iter[N].verdict`. Older state files (no
188	`.cycle_iterations` key) are upgraded in-place on the next write via
189	defensive `(.cycle_iterations //= {})` init in every mutator.
190	
191	### Step 3.5 — mid-cycle resume hand-off
192	
193	Inserted between the existing resume sequence's step 3 and step 4:
194	
195	> 3.5. If `cycle_iterations[X].status == in_progress`:
196	> - Re-validate the last completed stage's primary artifact via the
197	>   #496 validator. If missing → emit `cycle.iter.stale_artifact` and
198	>   re-run iter N from scratch (drop history rows for N, keep N-1).
199	> - If artifact present → resume between iters; start iter N+1 with
200	>   feedback already wired.
201	> - Restore `_cycle_history[]` from JSONL BEFORE plateau/divergence
202	>   eval; empty rehydration when `iter > 1` → emit `cycle.history.lost`
203	>   and fail closed (no silent coast).
204	
205	Without this hand-off, a `kill -9` during iter 2 of a 3-iter cycle would
206	restart from iter 1, losing progress and any cumulative state.
207	
208	## Amendment — atomic `.bak` rotation via `atomic_replace` (issue #909)
209	
210	The `.bak` rotation in `atomic_write` (the "Persisted" write path above) previously used
211	`cp "$target" "${target}.bak"` — a read + separate write — so a concurrent reader (or a crash
212	mid-copy) could observe a torn `.bak`. Because `.bak` is the **corruption-recovery source**
213	(the Resume sequence reads it on primary failure; `read_state`/`locked_state_update`/`validate_json`
214	restore from it), a torn backup silently defeats recovery — and the flock-less fallback in
215	`core/state/atomic.sh` makes this race live on systems without `flock`.
216	
217	Issue #909 introduces `atomic_replace <src> <dst>` (`scripts/lib/helpers.sh`): copy to a unique
218	temp **in dst's directory**, then `mv` (atomic rename on a POSIX filesystem). `atomic_write` now
219	rotates `.bak` via `atomic_replace`. The **contract is unchanged** — `.bak` remains the recovery
220	source and the Resume sequence is unchanged — but the guarantee is now stronger: a crash or
221	concurrent writer leaves either the old `.bak` or a complete new one, never a partial one. The
222	mirror-image recovery *restores* (`.bak`→target) are converted to the same primitive under #946.
223	
224	Issue #946 completes the pair: the three recovery restores — `validate_json` (`scripts/lib/helpers.sh`),
225	`read_state` and `locked_state_update`'s empty-recovery branch (`core/state/atomic.sh`) — previously
226	used a bare `cp "${x}.bak" "$x"`, so a reader holding no lock (notably `read_state`, called outside
227	the flock) could observe a torn target *during recovery*. All three now restore via `atomic_replace`,
228	and a failed restore **fails closed** (returns the corruption error) rather than reporting false
229	success on a still-corrupt file — closing a latent silent-failure the bare `cp` masked.
230	
231	## Implementation Notes (Phase 0.5 — issue #291)
232	
233	- **24h auto/manual resume boundary** is implemented at `core/state/resume.sh:178–199` (`age_seconds -lt 86400` → `auto_resume`, else `manual_resume_only`). Both BSD and GNU date parsing supported.
234	- **`current_iteration` persistence** is wired through `init_state()` (resume.sh:63 sets 0) and surfaces in the resume event at resume.sh:96.
235	- **Test coverage gaps tracked separately:** #299 (24h boundary not exercised), #300 (runner abort-trap state-write failure path not exercised by mutation A2).
236	- **Atomic `.bak` rotation (issue #909):** `atomic_write` rotates `.bak` via `atomic_replace` (`scripts/lib/helpers.sh`, temp+rename). Regression-guarded by `tests/unit/scripts-lib-atomic-replace-test.sh` (incl. a concurrent-reader negative control) and the 50× stability loop in `tests/integration/concurrent-state-test.sh`.
237	- **Atomic recovery restore (issue #946):** the three `.bak`→target restores (`validate_json` in `scripts/lib/helpers.sh`; `read_state` and the empty-recovery branch of `locked_state_update` in `core/state/atomic.sh`) restore via `atomic_replace` and fail closed on restore failure. Guarded by Case F (`[SPEC-3]`, a 12-writer concurrent-restore negative control proven to tear under bare `cp`) in `tests/unit/scripts-lib-atomic-replace-test.sh`, a `read_state` recovery case in `tests/unit/core-state-test.sh`, and Scenario 11 (complete large-`.bak` recovery) in `tests/integration/state-corruption-failclosed-b-test.sh`.
238	
239	## References
240	
241	- [KEEPERS.md §C correction: CURRENT_ITERATION lost on resume](../KEEPERS.md#section-c--reliability--safety-expanded)
242	- [KEEPERS.md §C addition 8: resume best-effort contract](../KEEPERS.md#additions-hidden-safety-primitives-the-original-spec-missed)

> **Memory type:** This ADR governs **pipeline-resume memory** — the operational
> state needed to continue an interrupted pipeline from where it stopped (which
> stage failed, which iteration counter, which checkpoint, scope manifest hash,
> plugin state, claim lease). It is one of zBuild's **two distinct memory models**:
>
> | Memory type | Purpose | Where defined | Backend |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | **Pipeline-resume memory** | Continue an interrupted pipeline at the failure point | ADR-006 (this), transported by ADR-010 cache | Always-on; baked into core/state/ |
> | **Learning memory** | Remember patterns, embeddings, decisions across pipelines and runs | [ADR-011](ADR-011-pluggable-backends.md) | Pluggable: sqlite default, ruflo HNSW optional |
>
> The two are independent: a pipeline can resume cleanly with no learning
> memory available, and learning memory persists across pipelines whether or
> not a particular pipeline ever resumed.

## Context

The legacy resume semantics are partially documented. `resume_state` in `legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-state.sh:876-1075` restores stage statuses and `SELF_HEAL_COUNT` but **does not** read back `CURRENT_ITERATION` — verified at line 269 (written) and confirmed absent in lines 987-1026 (read). On resume, plugins relying on iteration count receive the *initial* value (often 0), causing the loop to re-do iterations.

Other state that doesn't survive resume:
- `loop-state.md` (gitignored; per-iteration debug state; regenerated each run).
- Runtime caches (computed git diffs, environment snapshots, router recommendations).
- Scope-violation diagnostic logs (if `persist_artifacts` failed mid-write).

This isn't a bug per se; it's a contract that was never written down. Plugins inherit different assumptions: some assume iteration is durable; some assume it's reconstructed; some don't think about it at all. The result is brittle resume behavior.

## Decision

zBuild's resume contract is explicit. Two tiers: **persisted** (engine guarantees survival) and **reconstructed** (engine or plugin recomputes at the start of `run` after resume — ADR-056 deleted the `init` hook that used to own this).

### Persisted (engine-managed, atomic_write + .bak rotation)

| Key | Owner | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stage_statuses[]` | core/state | enum per stage | `pending`/`in_progress`/`complete`/`failed`/`skipped` |
| `current_iteration` | core/state | int | **NEW in zBuild** — fixes legacy resume gap |
| `self_heal_count` | core/state | int | per-stage retry counter |
| `scope_manifest_hash` | core/redaction | sha256 | detects scope-manifest mutation across resume |
| `cost_ledger_pointer` | core/cost | offset into ledger | enables resume to continue cost tracking |
| `plugin_state[plugin_id]` | per-plugin | opaque blob | plugin-declared state (see below) |
| `claim_lease_id` | core/locks | string | required for claim-coordinator's `heartbeat` after resume |
| ~~`events_db`~~ | core/event-bus | — | retired (amended 2026-10-24, ADR-065 §5): the SQLite mirror had no reader and was removed; the event history is `events.jsonl` |

All persisted state is written via `core/state/atomic_write`, which:
1. Disk-space precheck.
2. `flock` on a sidecar `.lock` file.
3. `mktemp` + write + `fsync`.
4. `mv` (atomic on POSIX).
5. Rotate previous to `.bak`.

> **Amended 2026-10-24 ([ADR-065](ADR-065-process-budget.md) §5).** No disk-space precheck: a full
> disk fails the write itself, which leaves the target untouched and says so. The temp file is
> opened by the shell with noclobber (exclusive, as `mktemp`'s was). The `.bak` is rotated only by
> the state writers (`atomic_write --bak`, used by `locked_state_update` and `init_state`), the
> only files the `.bak` recovery reads; other files keep no `.bak`.
>
> **Amended 2026-10-25 (ADR-065 §5, round 5).** The temp file is opened with the mode it must end
> with (the target's, or 0600 for a new file), so no `chmod` follows unless the mode has an
> execute bit. `atomic_replace` makes its unique temp name in the shell and claims it with
> noclobber, and copies with `cp -p`, so a state file's `.bak` keeps the state's 0600. Guarded by
> `tests/unit/atomic-write-cost-test.sh` W1/W3 and `tests/unit/helpers-cost-test.sh` H2/H3.

Reads use `validate_json`; corruption triggers `.bak` recovery. (KEEPERS §C additions 1–2 lift these into the hot path.)

### Reconstructed (computed at the start of `run` after resume)

| Key | Owner | How |
|---|---|---|
| `git_diff` | per-stage | `git diff` against baseline |
| `repo_hash` | core/state | hash of `git rev-parse HEAD` |
| `env_snapshot` | per-stage | captured in the `run` preamble |
| `router_recommendations` | core/router | recomputed from cost ledger + outcomes |
| `scope_violations_history` | per-stage | replayed from event bus |
| `loop_state_md` | debug | regenerated each iteration |

### Plugin responsibilities

Every plugin's `manifest.yaml` MUST declare:

```yaml
state:
  persisted: [findings, last_cycle_score]    # keys to write via core/state
  reconstructed: [git_diff, repo_hash]        # keys to recompute in the run preamble
```

The engine validates:
1. Every key in `persisted` has a corresponding `core/state/write_plugin_state <plugin_id> <key> <value>` call in `plugin.sh` (greppable; loose but catches obvious omissions).
2. Every key in `reconstructed` is set by the `run` preamble before the stage does any work. Asserted at runtime: missing keys → plugin refuses to run.

### Idempotency scope for `run`

"Plugins MUST be idempotent across re-runs of `run`" means:

- **In scope (A — what is guaranteed):** within a *single resume operation* on a *single pipeline-state.json*, the engine may call `run` more than once (e.g., the cycle re-enters the stage after a transient failure). The plugin MUST tolerate this: side-effects must be writable-or-reread without duplication. Concretely: writing to `core/state/write_plugin_state` is idempotent because the engine de-duplicates; writing to an external sink (Slack, GitHub comment) is NOT idempotent and MUST be guarded by a sentinel key in persisted state.
- **Out of scope (B — what is NOT guaranteed):** idempotency across *different* pipeline runs (run A resumes, then unrelated run B starts). Run B starts fresh; the plugin's `run` may legitimately re-emit side-effects from run B even if run A already did so. Cross-run de-duplication is the calling system's concern (e.g., GitHub issue body de-dup belongs in the output-destination layer, not in the plugin).

**Worked example.** `security-lens` declares `persisted: [last_pr_comment_id]`. On its first `run`, it posts a comment, captures the comment ID, writes it via `core/state/write_plugin_state`. On a second `run` *within the same resume*, it reads the persisted ID, sees the comment exists, skips the post. On a `run` for a different pipeline run, it has no persisted ID for that run and posts again — that's correct, because the runs are independent artifacts.

### Resume sequence

```
1. core/state load(pipeline-state.json) → on error: try .bak; on .bak error: refuse to resume
2. core/state restore persisted state into runtime
3. For each plugin in dependency order:
   a. call plugin.run with ZBUILD_RESUMING=1 (ADR-056 deleted the init hook;
      reconstruction is the run preamble's job)
   b. plugin reads persisted state via core/state/read_plugin_state
   c. plugin recomputes reconstructed state
   d. plugin refuses to continue if any reconstructed key is missing
4. Engine emits "pipeline.resume" event
5. Continue from last in_progress stage
```

### Best-effort contract

Resume is best-effort, not transparent. The engine guarantees:
- All `persisted` keys survive.
- All `reconstructed` keys are recomputed before any plugin observes them.
- If recomputation fails, the engine refuses to resume and exits with a clear error (no silent half-resume).

The engine does NOT guarantee:
- Identical behavior to an uninterrupted run (LLM nondeterminism makes this impossible).
- Cost equivalence (resume re-enters `run` and may re-route models).
- Wall-clock continuity (the resume adds startup latency).

## Consequences

**Good:**
- Fixes the legacy `CURRENT_ITERATION` resume gap explicitly.
- Plugin authors have a checklist: declare persisted, declare reconstructed, write tests.
- Resume failures are loud and explicit; no silent half-state.
- `kill -9` → restart works for any well-behaved plugin.

**Bad:**
- Manifest authorship friction (one more section to declare).
- Reconstructed state can be expensive to recompute (e.g., large git diffs). Mitigation: plugins can cache reconstructed state into persisted state if they declare both.
- The "every persisted key has a write_plugin_state call" check is grep-based, not type-checked. Accepted as a soft guardrail.

## Amendment — `preflight_failed` pipeline status (issue #496, ADR-020)

ADR-020 introduces a pre-flight inter-stage data contract validator that
runs at pipeline start (after `load_template`, before any stage executes).
When the validator fails in `ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce` mode, the
runner writes a minimal state.json with `status: preflight_failed` so
operators can distinguish "pipeline halted before any stage ran" from
"pipeline interrupted mid-flight."

The pipeline status enum now includes:

| Value | Set by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `in_progress` | runner | stages running |
| `complete` | runner | all stages succeeded |
| `interrupted` | runner | aborted mid-flight (signal, mid-stage failure) |
| `aborted` | runner / operator | explicit cancellation |
| `failed` | runner | terminal failure after at least one stage ran |
| `preflight_failed` | contract-validator (ADR-020) | rejected before any stage; no resume target |
| `timed_out` | runner watchdog (ADR-054 §11) | run exceeded per-run wall-clock limit; resumable |

Pipelines in `preflight_failed` status are NOT resumable; the runner's
resume policy refuses to restart them (the contract violation is in the
template or manifests, not in execution state). The resume command should
surface a "fix the contract first" hint rather than attempting to continue.

## Amendment — `cycle_iterations` persistence (issue #512, ADR-021)

ADR-021 introduces the outer-cycle orchestrator. Cycle state is persisted
under a new schema-additive key on `pipeline-state.json`:

```json
"cycle_iterations": {
  "<cycle_id>": {
    "status": "in_progress|complete|plateau|divergence|max_iterations|verdict_missing|aborted|preflight_failed",
    "current_iter": <N>,
    "max_iterations": <M>,
    "history_file": "<state_dir>/cycle-<id>-history.jsonl",
    "iter": [...]
  }
}
```

`stage_statuses[]` enum is **unchanged**. Per-cycle stage outcome lives
under `cycle_iterations[X].iter[N].verdict`. Older state files (no
`.cycle_iterations` key) are upgraded in-place on the next write via
defensive `(.cycle_iterations //= {})` init in every mutator.

### Step 3.5 — mid-cycle resume hand-off

Inserted between the existing resume sequence's step 3 and step 4:

> 3.5. If `cycle_iterations[X].status == in_progress`:
> - Re-validate the last completed stage's primary artifact via the
>   #496 validator. If missing → emit `cycle.iter.stale_artifact` and
>   re-run iter N from scratch (drop history rows for N, keep N-1).
> - If artifact present → resume between iters; start iter N+1 with
>   feedback already wired.
> - Restore `_cycle_history[]` from JSONL BEFORE plateau/divergence
>   eval; empty rehydration when `iter > 1` → emit `cycle.history.lost`
>   and fail closed (no silent coast).

Without this hand-off, a `kill -9` during iter 2 of a 3-iter cycle would
restart from iter 1, losing progress and any cumulative state.

## Amendment — atomic `.bak` rotation via `atomic_replace` (issue #909)

The `.bak` rotation in `atomic_write` (the "Persisted" write path above) previously used
`cp "$target" "${target}.bak"` — a read + separate write — so a concurrent reader (or a crash
mid-copy) could observe a torn `.bak`. Because `.bak` is the **corruption-recovery source**
(the Resume sequence reads it on primary failure; `read_state`/`locked_state_update`/`validate_json`
restore from it), a torn backup silently defeats recovery — and the flock-less fallback in
`core/state/atomic.sh` makes this race live on systems without `flock`.

Issue #909 introduces `atomic_replace <src> <dst>` (`scripts/lib/helpers.sh`): copy to a unique
temp **in dst's directory**, then `mv` (atomic rename on a POSIX filesystem). `atomic_write` now
rotates `.bak` via `atomic_replace`. The **contract is unchanged** — `.bak` remains the recovery
source and the Resume sequence is unchanged — but the guarantee is now stronger: a crash or
concurrent writer leaves either the old `.bak` or a complete new one, never a partial one. The
mirror-image recovery *restores* (`.bak`→target) are converted to the same primitive under #946.

Issue #946 completes the pair: the three recovery restores — `validate_json` (`scripts/lib/helpers.sh`),
`read_state` and `locked_state_update`'s empty-recovery branch (`core/state/atomic.sh`) — previously
used a bare `cp "${x}.bak" "$x"`, so a reader holding no lock (notably `read_state`, called outside
the flock) could observe a torn target *during recovery*. All three now restore via `atomic_replace`,
and a failed restore **fails closed** (returns the corruption error) rather than reporting false
success on a still-corrupt file — closing a latent silent-failure the bare `cp` masked.

## Implementation Notes (Phase 0.5 — issue #291)

- **24h auto/manual resume boundary** is implemented at `core/state/resume.sh:178–199` (`age_seconds -lt 86400` → `auto_resume`, else `manual_resume_only`). Both BSD and GNU date parsing supported.
- **`current_iteration` persistence** is wired through `init_state()` (resume.sh:63 sets 0) and surfaces in the resume event at resume.sh:96.
- **Test coverage gaps tracked separately:** #299 (24h boundary not exercised), #300 (runner abort-trap state-write failure path not exercised by mutation A2).
- **Atomic `.bak` rotation (issue #909):** `atomic_write` rotates `.bak` via `atomic_replace` (`scripts/lib/helpers.sh`, temp+rename). Regression-guarded by `tests/unit/scripts-lib-atomic-replace-test.sh` (incl. a concurrent-reader negative control) and the 50× stability loop in `tests/integration/concurrent-state-test.sh`.
- **Atomic recovery restore (issue #946):** the three `.bak`→target restores (`validate_json` in `scripts/lib/helpers.sh`; `read_state` and the empty-recovery branch of `locked_state_update` in `core/state/atomic.sh`) restore via `atomic_replace` and fail closed on restore failure. Guarded by Case F (`[SPEC-3]`, a 12-writer concurrent-restore negative control proven to tear under bare `cp`) in `tests/unit/scripts-lib-atomic-replace-test.sh`, a `read_state` recovery case in `tests/unit/core-state-test.sh`, and Scenario 11 (complete large-`.bak` recovery) in `tests/integration/state-corruption-failclosed-b-test.sh`.

## References

- [KEEPERS.md §C correction: CURRENT_ITERATION lost on resume](../KEEPERS.md#section-c--reliability--safety-expanded)
- [KEEPERS.md §C addition 8: resume best-effort contract](../KEEPERS.md#additions-hidden-safety-primitives-the-original-spec-missed)
- [ARCHITECTURE.md §4](../ARCHITECTURE.md#4-state-model) — full state model.
- `legacy-DoNotUse/scripts/lib/pipeline-state.sh:269` (write) vs `:987-1026` (read) — the gap this ADR closes.

`_prior_output_path` returns the path, and `prior_output_is_earlier_run` tells
the stage which kind it got.

### 6. Stage-authoring contract (what a new stage MUST do)

A plugin author, when creating or changing a stage, MUST observe:

- **Declare a primary artifact** (manifest `outputs:` with `primary: true`). That
  file — and only what the stage writes to the artifact area — is what gets
  snapshotted. The engine needs no per-stage code.
- **To reuse prior work**, read via `_read_prior_output` and treat the result as
  **advisory** ("reference, don't fully trust; verify against current inputs").
  Never skip the stage on the basis of prior output; never read pipeline/run state.
- **If the stage is a deterministic gate**, it MUST re-evaluate current state and
  MUST NOT reuse a prior verdict.
- **Never write anything that must not reach main into the work branch** — durable
  cross-run state belongs on the state branch (engine-managed), not in the code diff.

### 7. Amendment (#141) — git is the store, the folder is the working copy, and every run pushes

**Status:** Accepted (2026-08-23). See [ADR-059](ADR-059-issue-vs-run-keying.md) §3.

This ADR is already keyed by the issue, so ADR-059's layout does not compete with it. What ADR-059
settles is **which of the two is authoritative**, because there are now two places an issue's prior
work can live: the state branch above, and the on-disk `issues/<N>/artifacts/` directory.

**Git is the store. The folder is the working copy. On a disagreement, git wins.**

The disk is not a second store and does not gain independent authority by being closer to hand. It
is what a run reads and writes during its life; §2's branch is what survives it.

**The push moves out of CI and into the pipeline.** §4 says *"push the state branch once at the end,
pass or fail"*, and the #1878 amendments below add ordering and advisory-failure rules on top of it —
all of which read as engine behaviour. They are not. `core/state/artifact-persist.sh` has **no `git
push`**; it writes a local ref. The only state-branch push in the repository is a shell block in
`.github/workflows/zbuild-pipeline.yml`. A local run therefore snapshots to a branch nobody ever
sends anywhere, which is why #1921 measured hundreds of local commits and zero on origin.

ADR-059 §3 fixes this by making persistence a **stage** rather than engine code:

- **hydrate**, before intake — pulls the state branch into the folder. Git wins; it overwrites.
- **release**, at the end, **always-run**, short timeout — frees live resources, deletes nothing.
- **persist**, at the end after release, **always-run**, longer timeout — snapshots **and pushes**.

`_artifact_persist_restore` (`core/pipeline/runner.sh:1813`) becomes hydrate; the RUN-END snapshot
and the push become persist. This file stays as the shared library both stages source.

**Corrected 2026-08-23 (#1071).** An earlier draft said `_runner_snapshot_artifacts` "becomes
persist", which reads as moving it wholesale. §4's per-stage-boundary snapshots — six call sites —
are that section's own design and **stay engine-side**. The persist stage owns what never existed:
a final snapshot at run end, and the push. `_artifact_persist_push` is new in this file; nothing
in it has ever pushed before. The #1878 amendments survive intact and finally have somewhere to be enforced: the
push-order rule becomes stage order in the template, and the "advisory but never silent" rule
becomes the persist stage's own disposition.

**§3's exclusion is unchanged and gets no relaxation here.** Deterministic gate verdicts are still
*"always re-evaluated fresh"*. That rule exists because reuse produced **observed** false greens, and
a durable, pushed, cross-machine store makes stale-verdict leakage easier rather than harder.
Widening what may be reused is a separate decision from moving where work lives, and must not ride

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  zBuild core/state/artifact-persist — durable prior-run artifact store     ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Issue #1581. Generic, STAGE-AGNOSTIC persistence of a run's artifact area onto a
# SEPARATE state branch (`zbuild/state/issue-<N>`), so a later run of the same
# issue can pick prior work back up — locally or on a fresh CI runner where
# state/ is ephemeral. The store is a sibling branch that is NEVER part of the
# work branch's history, so it can never merge to main and never pollutes the PR
# diff (see #1581 design). This module knows nothing about individual stages or
# what any artifact means; it snapshots whatever files live in the artifact area.
#
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do NOT add set -euo here.
# All operations are best-effort: a failure returns non-zero but never aborts the
# run (callers treat persistence as advisory).


# #2010: zbuild_engine_tmpdir names where engine code writes temp files.
# Lazy-sourced, same pattern lifecycle.sh uses for stage-scratch.sh: this
# file is sourced from several entry points and cannot assume helpers.sh
# arrived first. helpers.sh sources only compat.sh, so there is no cycle.
if ! declare -F zbuild_engine_tmpdir_v >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/helpers.sh
    source "$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../../scripts/lib" && pwd)/helpers.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LOADED=1

    # the runner's stderr here, export ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_FD=3, and the
    # _stage_io_to_stdout renderer writes to that fd. The orch local engine's
    # `bash work-unit.sh > stdout 2> stderr` spawn touches only fd 1 and 2,
    # so fd 3 is inherited untouched by every plugin process.
    exec 3>&2

    # ── Determine skip-ahead point when --from-stage is set ───────────────────
    local skip_until_stage=""

    #   ZBUILD_CYCLES_ENABLED=1  → enabled (force on; explicit opt-in)
    #   unset + template has cycles[] → enabled (auto)
    #   else                       → disabled (no cycles in template anyway)
    # When auto-enabled, emit `cycle.auto_enabled` for observability.
    # When env=0 AND template has cycles, emit `cycle.disabled reason=env_override`

    local _template_has_cycle=0 _u

if [[ "$existing_status" == "aborted" ]] && ! $force; then
            error "Pipeline status is 'aborted'; use --force to resume anyway"
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ "$existing_status" == "complete" ]]; then
            warn "Pipeline status is 'complete'; starting fresh"
            resume_mode=false
        else
            # Restore run_id and issue from existing state
            _runner_run_id="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.run_id' "$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-$$")"
            _runner_issue="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.issue' '0')"
        fi
    elif ! $no_resume && [[ -f "$state_file" ]]; then
        # Auto-resume policy
        local recommendation
        recommendation="$(get_resume_recommendation "$state_file")"
        case "$recommendation" in
            auto_resume)
                info "Auto-resuming previous run (use --no-resume to force fresh start)"
                resume_mode=true
                _runner_run_id="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.run_id' "$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-$$")"
                _runner_issue="$(get_state_field "$state_file" '.issue' '0')"
                ;;
            manual_resume_only)
                info "Previous run requires explicit --resume (or --force for aborted)"
                resume_mode=false
                ;;
            fresh_start|*)
                resume_mode=false
                ;;
        esac
    fi

    if ! $resume_mode; then
        # Sanitize ZBUILD_RUN_ID: strip characters unsafe in filenames (/, .., spaces, etc.)
        # to prevent path traversal when run_id is used in report-${run_id}.md filenames
        # AND in the per-run state dir below (#887). Generated BEFORE the re-root.
        local _raw_run_id="${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-$$}"
        _runner_run_id="${_raw_run_id//[^a-zA-Z0-9_.-]/}"
        # Fall back to generated ID if sanitization emptied the value
        [[ -z "$_runner_run_id" ]] && _runner_run_id="$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)-$$"

        # switch landed kept the flat shape and nothing said so

        # state and are unaffected.
        _runner_issue="${issue:-0}"
        # #887: default state → isolate under runs/<run_id>/ so concurrent runs
        # never share artifacts. run_id is path-sanitized above. Done before
        # init_state so the per-run state file is the one created.
        if $_state_is_default; then
            # #141 (ADR-059 §1): nest the run under its ISSUE (or goal), so
            # everything for an issue lives in one place:

            # A run with no identity keeps the flat shape — there is nothing to
            # nest it under. Resolved through core/state/layout.sh so the
            # reclaimers read the same definition the writer uses.

# scripts/lib/lint-test-engine-state.sh refuses a hand-written one.

# Usage: zb_engine_loop_state <state_file> <loop id> <rounds> <limit> <final status>
zb_engine_loop_state() {
    local sf="$1" id="$2" rounds="$3" limit="$4" final="$5" root
    root="$(cd "${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true; cd "../.." && pwd)"
    ( source "$root/core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1

# Schema-additive: ensure .cycle_iterations[<cycle_id>] exists. Defensive init
# guards against older state files crashing on `.cycle_iterations` access
# (silent-failure finding #7).
_cycle_state_jq_init() {
    local _now; TZ=UTC0 printf -v _now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
    jq --arg id "$_ZB_CYCLE_ID" \
       --arg history "$_ZB_CYCLE_HISTORY" \
       --argjson max "$_ZB_CYCLE_MAX" \
       --arg now "$_now" \
       '(.cycle_iterations //= {})
        | (.cycle_iterations[$id] //= {
            status: "in_progress",
            current_iter: 0,
            max_iterations: $max,
            history_file: $history,
            iter: []
          })
        | .updated_at = $now'
}

_cycle_state_init() {
    local state_file="$1" cycle_id="$2" history_file="$3" max_iter="$4"
    export _ZB_CYCLE_ID="$cycle_id" _ZB_CYCLE_HISTORY="$history_file" \
           _ZB_CYCLE_MAX="$max_iter"
    locked_state_update "$state_file" "_cycle_state_jq_init" || return 1
    unset _ZB_CYCLE_ID _ZB_CYCLE_HISTORY _ZB_CYCLE_MAX
}

# ─── _cycle_state_write_iter_atomic ──────────────────────────────────────────
# Single atomic write per iter boundary (silent-failure finding #12).
# Updates: current_iter, iter[] append, status. NEVER split.
_cycle_state_jq_write_iter() {
    local _now; TZ=UTC0 printf -v _now '%(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)T' -1
    jq --arg id "$_ZB_CYCLE_ID" \
       --argjson n "$_ZB_CYCLE_N" \
       --arg verdict "$_ZB_CYCLE_VERDICT" \
       --arg status "$_ZB_CYCLE_ITER_STATUS" \
       --argjson fc "$_ZB_CYCLE_FC" \
       --arg overall "$_ZB_CYCLE_OVERALL" \
       --arg now "$_now" \
       '(.cycle_iterations //= {})
        | (.cycle_iterations[$id] //= {iter:[]})
        | .cycle_iterations[$id].current_iter = $n
        | .cycle_iterations[$id].status = $overall
        | .cycle_iterations[$id].iter += [{
              n: $n,
              status: $status,
              verdict: $verdict,
              failure_count: $fc,
              ended_at: $now
          }]
        | .updated_at = $now'
}

get_state_field() {
    local state_file="$1"
    local jq_path="$2"
    local default="${3:-}"
    if [[ ! -f "$state_file" ]]; then
        echo "$default"
        return 0
    fi
    # Validate and attempt .bak recovery before reading. rc=2 is unrecoverable
    # (main and .bak both corrupt, or the .bak restore itself failed) → default.
    # Suppress stderr — callers are read-only and must not be flooded by warnings.
    local _gsf_rc=0
    validate_json "$state_file" >/dev/null 2>&1 || _gsf_rc=$?
    if (( _gsf_rc == 2 )); then
        echo "$default"
        return 0
    fi
    local val
    val="$(jq -r "$jq_path // \"$default\"" "$state_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "$default")"
    echo "$val"

cycle_orchestrator_run() {
    local _cor_had_e=0 _cor_rc=0
    [[ $- == *e* ]] && _cor_had_e=1
    set +e
    _CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME=""; _CYCLE_LAST_MEMBER_HALT=""

    # A way out that named no outcome is read from its rc: success converged,

        if [[ $_cor_rc -eq 0 ]]; then _CYCLE_LAST_OUTCOME="converged"

# Build a tree from the artifact files under a stable prefix (artifacts/…),
    # plus a couple of top-level state docs, in a throwaway index.
    #
    # #1878: SKIP a file we cannot stage, do not abort the snapshot. This loop
    # used to `break` on the first failure, discarding every artifact already
    # staged — while the `extra` loop below has always skipped-and-continued. A
    # file that vanished mid-scan (the artifact area has live writers) or is
    # unreadable must cost us that one file, not the whole snapshot.
    local added=0 skipped=0 f rel blob first_skip="" n
    local -a _abs=() _rel=()
    while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        _abs+=("$f"); _rel+=("artifacts/${f#"$art_dir"/}")
    done < <(find "$art_dir" -type f -print0 2>/dev/null)
    # Include a handful of top-level state docs when present (scope manifest etc.).
    local extra
    for extra in scope-manifest.md intake.md; do
        [[ -f "$state_dir/$extra" ]] || continue
        _abs+=("$state_dir/$extra"); _rel+=("$extra")
    done

    # #2249: two git calls for the whole set — `hash-object --stdin-paths` and
    # `update-index --index-info` — instead of two per file (a run snapshots
    # after every stage, over hundreds of files). Any failure in the batch (an
    # unreadable file aborts hash-object) falls back to the per-file loop below,
    # so #1878's rule holds: a file we cannot stage costs only that file.
    if _artifact_persist_stage_batch "$_gd" "$tmp_index"; then
        added=${#_abs[@]}
    else
        rm -f "$tmp_index"
        for (( n = 0; n < ${#_abs[@]}; n++ )); do
            f="${_abs[$n]}"; rel="${_rel[$n]}"
            if ! blob="$(GIT_DIR="$_gd" git hash-object -w "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; then
                skipped=$((skipped + 1)); [[ -z "$first_skip" ]] && first_skip="$rel (hash-object)"
                continue
            fi

            if ! GIT_INDEX_FILE="$tmp_index" GIT_DIR="$_gd" \

            added=$((added + 1))
        done

    # and lost it); if there were simply no files, it is an honest empty.
    if [[ "$added" -eq 0 ]]; then
        rm -f "$tmp_index"

            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
            _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="all $skipped file(s) unstageable, first: $first_skip"
            return 1

        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="no files under $art_dir"

    local _vpp
    _verdict_primary_output_path_v _vpp "${1-}"

}

# over when the outputs block closes and reopens, as they did in the awk.
_verdict_primary_output_path_v() {
    local -n _vpo="$1"; _vpo=""
    local manifest="${2-}" l v in_out=0 cpath="" cprim=""
    [[ -f "$manifest" && -r "$manifest" ]] || return 0
    declare -F _mg_clean_v >/dev/null 2>&1 \
        || source "$_ZBUILD_VERDICT_ROOT/scripts/lib/manifest-graph.sh"
    local re_open='^outputs:' re_top='^[a-zA-Z_]' re_id='^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*id:'
    local re_kv='^[[:space:]]+(path|primary):'
    while IFS= read -r l || [[ -n "$l" ]]; do
        [[ "$l" =~ $re_open ]] && { in_out=1; continue; }
        [[ "$l" =~ $re_top ]] && in_out=0
        (( in_out )) || continue
        if [[ "$l" =~ $re_id ]]; then
            [[ "$cprim" == "true" && -n "$cpath" ]] && { _vpo="$cpath"; return 0; }
            cpath=""; cprim=""; continue
        fi
        if [[ "$l" =~ $re_kv ]]; then
            v="${l#*:}"; _mg_strip_lead_v v; _mg_clean_v v
            if [[ "${BASH_REMATCH[1]}" == path ]]; then cpath="$v"; else cprim="$v"; fi
        fi
    done 2>/dev/null < "$manifest"
    [[ "$cprim" == "true" && -n "$cpath" ]] && _vpo="$cpath"
    return 0
}

_runner_now_ms() {
